MINUTES
  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  JUNE 3, 2020

CHAIR SCHMITZ called the meeting of the Environmental Advisory Committee of the City of
Rolling Hills Estates to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  SCHMITZ, BACINSKI, RADOCCHIO, STEGURA,
  UPPAL, YOO*

COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  CHAN-SOUTHWELL, BAIN, LARSON,
  SCHACHTER

STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  ALEXA DAVIS, ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER
  JEANNIE NAUGHTON, PLANNING MANAGER
  CAROL COREA, ADMINISTRATIVE ASSISTANT

* ALTERNATE FOR COMMITTEE MEMBER SCHACHTER

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING, FEBRUARY
  20, 2020

The Committee Members moved to approve,

  THE ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF FEBRUARY
  20, 2020

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS/ORAL COMMUNICATION ON ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  CONSIDERATION OF THE PROHIBITION OF GASOLINE-POWERED LEAF BLOWERS

Planning Manager Naughton provided a summary of the staff report. She explained the
environmental effects for the emissions and dust. In addition, there are significant concerns from
the noise relating to hearing loss. In regards to the concern that leaf blowers contribute to the
spread of COVID-19; staff received a statement from the LA County Department of Public Health
stating that there is no scientific evidence to show that leaf blowers spread COVID-19.

Planning Manager Naughton stated that there are cities, such as Carmel by the Sea and Beverly
Hills, that have banned leaf blowers categorizing them as a public nuisance due to the noise
impact. There are other cities, such as Rolling Hills Estates, that regulates leaf blowers using time
restrictions. Rancho Palos Verdes bans the use of gas-powered leaf blowers for single-family
residences. There are also cities that are banning gas-powered leaf blowers but allowing electric
blowers and there are some cities that ban leaf blowers all together.

The South Coast Air Quality Management District has been offering two rebate programs to
replace residential gas-powered lawn mowers for electric lawn mowers, and a commercial
program for replacement of gas-powered lawn and garden equipment.

This program was brought up to the Rolling Hills Country Club and they have electrified 70% of
their lawn and garden equipment.

There is concern with the large commercial and school districts to be able to electrify their
equipment. The City’s landscape contractor, Bennett, uses gas-powered leaf blowers and per a
discussion with them, they are not in a position to electrify their equipment at this time. The South
Coast Air Quality Management District rebate program may be something that they could use to

 ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  1
 MINUTES, JUNE 3, 2020
 swap out their equipment. In addition, if the City were to ban gas-powered leaf blowers, there may
be a need to modify the contract with Bennett.

Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff provided the following recommendations:

  1.  Complete gas leaf blower ban throughout the City (electric blowers may be used).

  2.  Prohibit gas leaf blowers in single-family residential districts only (use may
  continue on properties zoned for multi-family, commercial, and institutional uses).

  3.  Prohibit gas and electric leaf blowers either citywide or in residential districts only.

  4.  Continue to enforce noise and time of day restrictions for leaf blowers (allowing
  both gas and electric leaf blowers).

Assistant City Manager Davis added that Palos Verdes Estates also has a ban on gas-powered
leaf blowers for single-family residences.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI stated that recommendation two, which prohibits gas leaf
blowers in single-family residential districts only, seems like a reasonable option.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA inquired about the City of Beverly Hills ban on leaf blowers.
Planning Manager Naughton stated that their ban on both gas and electric leaf blowers went into
effect in the mid 1970’s and classified them as a public nuisance.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA stated that her electric leaf blower is louder than gas-powered
leaf blowers.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA stated that not all homeowners hire gardeners and this ban
would affect everyone in the City. She asked her own gardener about a ban on gas-powered leaf
blowers and he stated that electric leaf blowers are not as powerful as the gas-powered leaf
blowers and would need to charge it at every home. She stated that she would like to get more
input on this item.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA stated that if the rationale for allowing an exemption for the
Rolling Hills Country Club because they are next to homes, and they need time to electrify their
equipment, then the same should go for the school district sites, which also have homes adjacent
to them.

COMMITTEE MEMBER UPPAL stated that she agrees with recommendation two, which prohibits
gas leaf blowers in single-family residences only. However, she expressed her concern with the
cost of buying additional batteries if charging is not an option at every home that needs to be
serviced.

COMMITTEE MEMBER RADOCCHIO stated that they would save money on fuel. He stated that
his neighbor has an electric leaf blower and he can barely hear it.

COMMITTEE MEMBER RADOCCHIO stated that in reference to the letter that was submitted, it
states that the leaf blower could be used for an hour and stated that his yard is fairly large and
they only use the leaf blower for 10 minutes at the most. He also agreed that more input is needed.

COMMITTEE MEMBER YOO stated that there are battery powered and wired options that may
vary in power and noise levels; however, he still believes that electric powered may be weaker
than gas-powered leaf blowers. He asked if there has been any consideration in allowing seasonal
exceptions, such as allowing gas leaf blowers in the fall. Planning Manager Naughton stated that
there are cities who only allow them during certain seasons of the year.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI stated that he owns an electric leaf blower and has had no
problems with and it is quieter than the gas-powered leaf blower.

CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that she is the gardener in her family and stated that she uses an electric
leaf blower and it is quite powerful and quieter than a gas-powered leaf blower. When she is using
it, it is for approximately 10 minutes.

CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that we only have input from the City’s contractor and feedback from our
own maintenance staff, so she is concerned for the fleet of residential, commercial, school district
and other individuals providing services and would like to get their input.

 ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  2
 MINUTES, JUNE 3, 2020
 COMMITTEE STEGURA stated that she would abstain, absent the input from the people who
use gas leaf blowers and recommends that we get more input.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI made a motion to approve option two as presented in the staff
report.

CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that there being no second to the motion, the motion fails.

CHAIR SCHMITZ directed staff to contact the landscape contractor for the schools in Rolling Hills
Estates, the HOAs to gain feedback from homeowners who are their own gardeners, and the fleet
of small business gardeners that service the City.

In response to a question from COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA, Assistant City Manager Davis
stated that staff can coordinate with the HOAs, put a survey together than can be completed
online, and suggest that residents talk to their gardeners directly and provide input. This would
also provide an opportunity to gather input from the commercial and school districts.

In response to a comment by COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI, Chair Schmitz stated that the
purpose of requesting input would not be how they feel about gas versus electric; instead to gauge
the onerous, monetary and manpower effects this would have on a fleet.

COMMITTEE MEMBER YOO asked what the City of Beverly Hills uses in place of leaf blowers.
Planning Manager Naughton stated that they may be doing the work manually.

COMMITTEE MEMBER UPPAL asked about enforcement. Planning Manager Naughton stated
enforcement would be a considerable challenge.

Planning Manager Naughton thanked the Committee for allowing staff additional time to speak
with the various stakeholders, to provide input for the next meeting.

A brief discussion was held regarding the next meeting. Staff stated that a few weeks would be
needed to prepare for the next meeting and recommended that the next meeting be held in mid-
July.

CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that the order of the committee will be to continue Item 5A, consideration
of the prohibition of gasoline-powered leaf blowers, to the next Environmental Advisory
Committee meeting.

6.  STAFF ITEMS

NONE

7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

CHAIR SCHMITZ reminded everyone to check the City’s website on what a good earthquake kit
should include.

COMMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI reminded everyone to keep a wrench near your gas meter
in case of an emergency.

COMMITTEE MEMBER RADOCCHIO stated that a sensor can be installed on your gas line that
will shut off your gas if there is a major earthquake.

CHAIR SCHMITZ thanked everyone for attending.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting at 7:45 p.m.
